title: Sprint execution_state.json schema
description: Validates claude/cycles/<cycle_id>/execution_state.json — introduced to make CLAUDE.md §8 step 2b (shared-JSON-field schema-shape drift) partly CI-checked instead of purely manual. Tested against all 73 historical execution_state.json files under claude/cycles/ before being wired into CI (see claude/schemas/README.md for the validation run). That history showed the top-level envelope, per-epic fields, and even per-story fields (e.g. `delivery_note`, `sign_off_record`) legitimately gain new one-off fields and shapes release to release — a single engine evolving its own output over time, not the concurrent-sibling-branch risk §8 2b describes. Locking those with additionalProperties:false produced constant false positives against real history, so this schema stays additionalProperties:true throughout and only type-checks the *known* fields when present (catches a field being silently repurposed to a different JSON type — e.g. `status` becoming a number — without fighting organic field growth). The one place additionalProperties:false is used is `trackedItemEntry` (blocked_items/delegated_items entries): that shape validated 100% clean across all 73 historical files despite real historical variety (plain ST-id strings, EPIC-qualified strings, free-text status strings, and — in v4.0 — a full object), so it is the one part of this schema precise enough to safely reject an unreviewed new shape. The true concurrent-branch case (two sibling EPIC branches independently adding the *same new field name* with *different* shapes, which this static schema cannot see since neither shape is 'known' yet) is instead caught by the separate sibling-branch diff job in execution-state-schema-check.yml — see that workflow's own comments.

trackedItemEntry.description: blocked_items / delegated_items entries. Accepts the real historical shapes (bare ST-id, EPIC-qualified ST-id, free-text status string, or the v4.0-style detail object) but rejects any other object shape, so a new shape must be added here deliberately rather than slip through a clean merge. Validated 100% clean across all 73 historical execution_state.json files — the one field in this schema precise enough to be additionalProperties:false without false positives.
